beats.text: Anthropologists looked at a hundred and sixty-eight cultures around the world.
Romantic kissing showed up in fewer than half.
Every culture they studied in the Middle East did it. In South America, only four out of thirty-three.
And among hunter-gatherers, there was little sign of it at all.
So the kiss isn't universal. It's culture. Which makes it a little more special.

sources: Jankowiak, Volsche & Garcia (2015). Is the romantic-sexual kiss a near human universal? American Anthropologist 117(3). 168 cultures; ~46% with romantic-sexual kissing; Middle East 10/10, Europe 7/10, North America 18/33, South America 4/33; little evidence among foragers. Via ScienceAlert.
